newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat-Netanyahu summit set on Hebron - U.S..
newsitem.headline: Arafat-Netanyahu summit set on Hebron - U.S..

text.p: The leaders of Israel and the Palestinians will meet late on Tuesday to try to break a deadlock over Israeli troop redeployments in the West Bank, a U.S. envoy said.
"We have been working and there will be a meeting tonight between the prime minister and the chairman at Erez. It'll be a late-night meeting," mediator Dennis Ross told Israel Radio.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office, asked about a summit, said in a statement: "It could be but it hasn't been finalised."
Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, chairman of the PLO, would meet at the Erez crossing between Israel and the self-ruled Gaza Strip.
Arafat's adviser said earlier the Palestinian leader was ready to meet Netanyahu to remove obstacles holding up a deal to extend Palestinian rule to the West Bank town of Hebron.
